title: Correct exit angle
description: Essential: The student must state the final refraction angle as 45° (or equivalent in radians).

title: Correct travel time
description: Essential: The student must provide the final time expression as (5√2 a)/(√3 c) or an equivalent simplified form.

title: Critical angle calculation
description: Important: The student must correctly calculate the critical angle θ_c = arcsin(1/n) = 45° to determine that total internal reflection does not occur at the first glass-air interface.

title: Internal incidence angle
description: Important: The student must correctly use geometry (e.g., prism angles and normal lines) to find the angle of incidence at the exit face (30°).

title: Snell's law application
description: Important: The student must apply Snell's law (n sin(i) = sin(r)) correctly at the exit interface to find the refraction angle.

title: Path length determination
description: Important: The student must correctly calculate the total optical path length inside the prism using geometry (e.g., distances along the two internal segments).

title: Speed in medium
description: Optional: The student should explicitly state the speed of light in the prism as v = c/√2.

title: Unit consistency
description: Optional: The final time expression should have correct units (e.g., seconds) implied by the dimensional variables a and c.

title: Misapplied total internal reflection
description: Pitfall: Penalize if the student incorrectly assumes total internal reflection occurs at the first glass-air interface (60° > 45° is true, but the light is not incident there in this geometry).

title: Geometry or Snell's law error
description: Pitfall: Penalize for significant errors in prism geometry (e.g., wrong incidence angle at exit face) or misapplication of Snell's law (inverting n).
